newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates dip on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates dip on low demand.

text.p: Pakistan cotton rates dipped on Monday as low demand from spinners prompted ginners to unload stocks before the arrival of the 1997/98 (July-June) crop, dealers said.
"Ginners are sitting on large unsold stocks," dealer Mustafa Hussain said. Prices may edge lower if major buyers do not enter the market at these levels, he added.
The Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association said 1996/97 output had reached a provisional 8.761 million 375-lb bales by May 1, down from 9.938 million at the same time a year ago.
